convoLines.text: "I asked Amara about the pantry run — Amara's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the burdock patch past the treeline and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"White Noise — The heron is gone. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"Amara owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on how you slept. You know?"
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? …sorry."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Amara always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Amara's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."

"It's my grandmother, Diwa. Was taken. Eighty-one years old and they called her boring. Eighty-one years. The pods get into my sleep some nights. Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Since Amara died... I keep expecting to see Amara at the fire. Stupid."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I keep turning over the last thing Amara said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Wild Strawberry — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about how you slept — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'Forget I said anything. What did you want? …sorry.'"
"Take your time."
"Still on that question."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"That's the whole of it. Sorry."

"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"The fire's the real leader here. We just orbit it and pretend we're in charge."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"Here. I made an extra." Lillian presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"It crouches low, tail lashing once, twice. That's The Mountain Lord telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Asian Persimmon. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."

"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Jacob — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Alright — I should get back to it."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Duel. They just... took Jacob. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I pace while thinking. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Same as always: we endure."

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Amara Yang is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Amara Yang is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Amara — and Amara is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: 🧳 Word from Stonebridge: Tomás was killed — Andre did it, they say. (The truth: dead is dead; the killing part is gossip.)
d42: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. The Big Beast is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Amara home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Mai, Lillian, Jacob and 5 more speak for Wanjiru — "Amara trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d41: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Fully identify 3 plants (knowledge level 3) within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
burialWindowSay: d41: The village's quarrel was with Amara — and Amara is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Mai, Lillian, Jacob and 5 more speak for Wanjiru — "Amara trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
d41: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
d42: That night, they bring Amara home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d42: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)
d44: You say a few words for Amara. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d44: Burying the bloating dead was honest work, and it cost you. Fever by nightfall. (-10 health)
d44: You bury Amara. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+5 trauma)
echoSample: d44: "I asked Amara about the pantry run — Amara's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
d44: "Amara owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d44: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Amara always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d44: "Nobody says Amara's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d44: "Since Amara died... I keep expecting to see Amara at the fire. Stupid."
d44: "I keep turning over the last thing Amara said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
echoV2Sample: d42: You take branch, bark strip, stick, stone, stick, audience token, stick, system field manual: small game (rev. 5), stick, fan care package (unopened), stone knife from Amara. Your hands know what they did. (+11 trauma)
d44: The village raises a marker by the fire — Amara, day 44. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
